title: AgentMail + HydraDB: Persistent AI Agent Memory for Your Inbox
summary: Sync AgentMail inboxes into HydraDB so your AI agent can recall past email, threads and attachments before it replies. Setup takes one command.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


AgentMail now integrates with HydraDB, the open-source context and memory layer for AI agents. A small Python connector syncs your AgentMail inboxes into HydraDB, so your agent can search its past email before it replies, with threads and reply chains kept intact. Setup is one pip install, three environment variables and one sync command.


Email is where an agent's working history piles up. The price a customer accepted, the contract version they signed off on, the follow-up they asked for three weeks ago: it all sits in the inbox. Most agents only ever see the message in front of them, though. Each run starts cold, and anything outside the current thread is invisible unless you build retrieval yourself.


Today we're shipping an integration with[HydraDB](https://hydradb.com/) that gives your agent persistent memory over its inbox. HydraDB is a context and memory layer for AI agents, built as an open-source graph database. The[hydradb-agentmail-plugin](https://github.com/hydra-db/hydradb-agentmail-plugin) connector syncs an AgentMail inbox into HydraDB as an app source. When your agent asks "what pricing did we agree on?", it gets back the email that answers the question along with the conversation around it.


## What does the AgentMail and HydraDB integration do?


The connector copies the email in your AgentMail inboxes into a HydraDB database. Your agent still sends and receives through AgentMail exactly as before. HydraDB is where it searches when it needs to remember something from an older thread. You can sync a single inbox or every inbox on your account.


For each message, the connector stores:


- The subject and body text, plus sender, recipients, labels and attachment names and types
- A link to its thread, and a link to the message it replied to
- The inbox and thread IDs as metadata, so you can scope recall to one agent's mail


Messages are keyed on their RFC Message-ID. Running the sync again updates a message instead of duplicating it, and reply links still connect when the parent and the reply arrive in different sync runs.


## What can you build with agent email memory?


**Support agents that check history first.** Before answering a ticket, the agent pulls the customer's earlier threads and sees what was already promised, tried or escalated.


**Sales and ops agents that remember terms.** Quotes, delivery dates and agreed exceptions live in email. The agent can recall them by meaning ("what discount did Acme get?") rather than by exact subject line.


**Assistants that run for weeks.** Synced email stays searchable across agent runs, so an assistant that wakes up on a schedule picks up where it left off. If you're already using HydraDB for Slack, docs or a CRM, email becomes one more source in the same query.


## How do I set up AgentMail with HydraDB?


You need an[AgentMail account](https://console.agentmail.to/) with an API key (free to start), a[HydraDB account](https://dashboard.hydradb.com/) with an API key and a target database, and Python 3.9 or later.


Install the connector:


Bash


```text
pip     install     hydradb-agentmail-plugin
```


Set your keys and the HydraDB database to write into:


Bash


```text
export     AGENTMAIL_API_KEY  =  "  your-agentmail-key  "   export     HYDRADB_API_KEY  =  "  your-hydradb-key  "   export     HYDRADB_DATABASE  =  "  your-database  "
```


Sync every inbox on the account, or pass one inbox to scope it:


Bash


```text
agentmail-sync   agentmail-sync     agent@agentmail.to
```


Then query HydraDB. With` query_apps` on (the default), synced email is searched alongside any other app sources in the database:


Bash


```text
curl     https://api.hydradb.com/query     \       -H     "  Authorization: Bearer $HYDRADB_API_KEY  "     \       -H     "  API-Version: 2  "     \       -H     "  Content-Type: application/json  "     \       -d     '  {"database": "your-database", "query": "what pricing did we agree on?", "query_apps": true}  '
```


Results come back with the source email and its thread and reply relationships, ready to drop into your agent's prompt.


## How do I keep the agent's memory current?


There are two options, and most teams use both.


For backfill, run` agentmail-sync` on a schedule. Set` AGENTMAIL_AFTER` to an ISO 8601 timestamp to pull only messages after a cutoff, which keeps each run incremental.


For real-time memory, ingest each email as it arrives. Subscribe to the` message.received` and` message.sent`[webhook events](https://docs.agentmail.to/events) and call the connector's` message_to_item` and` ingest_items` functions from your handler. The agent can then recall a message seconds after it lands.


If you run many agents or customers from one HydraDB database, set` HYDRADB_COLLECTION` to give each one its own sub-tenant scope.


The full reference lives in our[HydraDB integration docs](https://docs.agentmail.to/integrations/hydradb) , and the connector source is on[GitHub](https://github.com/hydra-db/hydradb-agentmail-plugin) .
